/-! # Woodall Primes

References:
* [Wikipedia/Woodall Number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodall_number#Woodall_primes)
* [A2234](https://oeis.org/A2234)

-/

namespace WoodallPrimes

/-- There are infinitely many prime numbers of the form `k * 2 ^ k - 1` for `k > 1`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinitely_many_woodall_primes : {k : ℕ | 1 < k ∧ (k * 2 ^ k - 1).Prime}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end WoodallPrimes

reformulations.difference: Lean asserts infinitude of the qualifying indices k > 1, whereas Wikipedia asks for infinitely many distinct Woodall prime values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive k, W(k) = k * 2^k - 1 is strictly increasing, so the map from qualifying indices to Woodall prime values is a bijection. Excluding k = 1 loses no prime because W(1) = 1. Natural-number subtraction agrees with ordinary subtraction throughout the permitted domain. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, indices_equiv_prime_values proves the equivalence with infinitude of {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ p = k * 2^k - 1}; separate proofs check the domain restriction and subtraction.
